# Thomas Kabalin

> Third-year Bachelor of Business Science (Computer Science) student at UCT, currently ranked first across the Computer Science cohort, and Junior Software Engineer at a Cape Town fintech. Sitting at the intersection of technology and business, with interests in software engineering, data science, AI, consulting, and quantitative finance.

Thomas Kabalin is a South African student and software engineer based in Cape Town, South Africa. As of 2026, he is in his third year of a Bachelor of Business Science (Computer Science) degree at the University of Cape Town (UCT), a four-year programme, with an expected graduation year of 2027. He is currently ranked first across the Computer Science cohort, with a first-year GPA of 88.13 and a second-year GPA of 85.68. He combines strong technical and analytical ability with a commercial mindset, and is drawn to using AI as a practical tool to build faster and automate manual processes.

Academic awards include the Vice-Chancellor's Scholarship (top 10 applicants from the Western Cape), the BSG Prize for the top second-year Computer Science student, the Bain & Company Award (3rd place, first-year BBusSci), class medals as the top-ranked student in CSC1016S (Object-Oriented Programming, ~800 students), STA2020F (Applied Statistics, ~520 students), and CSC2002S (Computer Science 2B, ~430 students), and the Dean's Merit List for 2024 and 2025. He matriculated from Cannons Creek High School as Dux Scholar with a 96.3% aggregate, 8 distinctions (three at 99%, all above 90%), and a Silver Medal in the South African Computer Applications Olympiad (top 3 of ~18,300).

He works part-time as a Junior Software Engineer at Fynbos Technologies, a Cape Town-based fintech company, where he builds and ships backend features in PHP and Laravel. There he built a bank reconciliation system that auto-matches ~81% of transactions (replacing manual spreadsheet matching previously done by senior staff) and a direct-to-bank withdrawal feature that removes a manual step for customers, applying prompt, context, and memory engineering to orchestrate and critically review AI-generated code. He has also run a digital study materials business since 2021, developing practical skills in sales, marketing, and independent business operations.

Technical proficiencies include Java, Python, PHP (Laravel), and C#, with working knowledge of SQL, HTML, CSS, and R. He has extensive experience integrating AI tools and LLM-assisted workflows across academic, professional, and personal contexts.

Previously, he completed a data science job shadow at Prescient Investment Management, where he built a machine learning model estimating U.S. recession probabilities using the Treasury yield curve. His consulting exposure includes attendance at the McKinsey Tech & AI Roundtable, as well as participation in the Deloitte Young Executives Programme. In the computing olympiad community, he serves as one of two national External Moderators for the South African Applications Olympiad and Talent Search (2026–present), competitions reaching over 50,000 participants annually, and as a Scientific Committee member for the South African Programming Olympiad (2024–present), designing and reviewing algorithmic problems whose winners represent the country at the International Olympiad in Informatics.

His professional interests span software engineering, data science, the practical applications of AI, quantitative development, business innovation, and technology-driven problem solving. He is actively exploring careers at the intersection of technology and business, including consulting, finance, and software engineering roles.
